overview.text: ZCG's announcement (#1) offers to taper its funding to the 2032 halving, return about 36,200 ZEC from its treasury and fill the NSM instead, and polls on a full proposal. A few replies back it as a good direction or middle ground (#2, #11, #72), while critics say it misses the point: it ignores coinholder representation and accountability, extends ZCG's mandate to 2032 and still leaves a large sum (#3, #4, #9, #52).

A long exchange centres on ZSAs. maxdesalle and thailand85 argue ZCG funded a $455K grant after 98.6% voted against ZSAs (#4, #13, #22, #27, #33). artkor, hanh and wobbzz answer that the poll was advisory and asked about ZSAs as a protocol feature, and that the grant adapts and merges existing code (#18, #25, #26, #40). vinibarbosa, wobbzz, emersonian and skyl add that 98.6% reflects participating coin weight at low turnout (#20, #40, #41, #69). A dispute over the wording shown in a wallet screenshot follows (#30, #33, #37), and strahncryptography tells artkor that maxdesalle is right (#38).

Participants also argue over who owns the money and who should govern it. Critics hold that coinholders pay and should control it, and that committees cannot work (#3, #4); strahncryptography, vinibarbosa and wobbzz reply that miners pay under ZIP 1016, the allocation belongs to ZCG by protocol, and independent funding channels are deliberate (#11, #12, #24, #40). Batuhan, emersonian, wobbzz and Milton counter that coin-weighted voting is itself open to whales and hostile actors (#23, #39, #45, #73).

The thread turns personal around maxdesalle's employer: Samriddha and emersonian allege his campaign serves his employer (#14, #41), he denies it and calls the insult low (#46), and emersonian answers with a hostile post alleging funding capture (#47). Earlier, strahncryptography pointed to Cypherpunk's own committees and thailand85 and maxdesalle replied that those are privately funded and legally required (#8, #13, #16, #17).

Alternatives and track record fill the middle of the thread. ValarDragon suggests a USD cap (#28); strahncryptography proposes ending the subsidy and restructuring ZCG, which thailand85 would support depending on details and seernet calls better than the current structure but unlikely to pass (#53, #57, #58, #63, #64). strahncryptography lists projects ZCG funded (#50) and mrkit2u defends red-bridge (#59, #67, #68), while thailand85, seernet and dogemos say the list shows little adoption (#54, #60, #61, #75). seernet says he has been radicalized and wants ZCG disbanded (#74).

Later posts widen the frame: skyl wants the committee wound down but dev funding kept large and protocol-governed (#69), zcashminer1 diagnoses structural flaws and argues for fixing rather than abolishing ZCG (#76), and kworks and gordonesTV push regional reserves (#78, #81). strahncryptography points to ebfull's proposal as satisfying everyone, and fabacab replies that most of the community does not know it exists (#79, #80).

positions.label: Support the taper as a workable compromise
positions.summary: ZCG gives up funding it does not need: it tapers its share to the 2032 halving, donates part of its treasury and fills the NSM, keeping the 20% total and the program running. Supporters see a good direction and a middle ground that could calm the governance conflict, and want the full proposal before deciding.

positions.label: The taper is not enough: end ZCG and its block-reward subsidy
positions.summary: Coinholders pay for ZCG without representation, ZCG funded ZSAs against their vote, committees cannot work and the proposal even extends ZCG to 2032, so the subsidy should end or ZCG should be abolished. dans (ZODL, disclosed) also opposes the proposal as not solving the issue.

positions.label: Restructure ZCG for accountability instead of dissolving it
positions.summary: The problem is ZCG's structure and incentives, not protocol-level funding. End the subsidy or make it conditional, move to a legally accountable structure with defined goals and named managers, and keep the capital working.

positions.label: Community grants are legitimate; coin-weighted voting is no safer
positions.summary: The ZCG allocation is set by ZIPs and does not belong to coinholders; independent channels are deliberate; coin-weighted votes are held by amount-holders, can be captured by whales or hostile actors, and are not a neutral alternative. Scrutiny of ZCG is fine, but both models deserve the same standard.

positions.label: The ZSA poll was advisory and the grant preserved funded work
positions.summary: The poll asked for sentiment on including ZSAs as a protocol feature (in NU7), was described as advisory, and was weighted by participating coins at low turnout; the grant adapts and merges existing code, so ZCG did not defy a binding decision. wobbzz still says continued ZSA spending needs an explanation.

positions.label: ZCG's record is substantial
positions.summary: Critics fixate on two or three grants and ignore hundreds of others; ZCG funded wallets, hardware support, Arti, bridges and integrations, and the red-bridge grant brought in about $2M of pledges.

positions.label: ZCG's record is poor and its budget is being misused
positions.summary: The funded items have little adoption or impact, ZSAs were a failure, and large budgets invite further mistakes, so it is best to fix things now.

positions.label: Keep large, continuing dev funding, governed at the protocol level
positions.summary: Zcash still has much to build and no war chest is too big; the committee model should be wound down in favour of granular, accountable, protocol-governed awards, and statistics used in the thread (98.6%, 96.6%) are often misleading on both sides.

positions.label: Slow down and widen who is included
positions.summary: The plan is premature and needs at least a month of debate and more polling; proposals should not be said to satisfy 'everyone' while most of the community, including people who are not current stakeholders, has not seen them.

positions.label: Other proposals: a USD cap, regional reserves, ebfull's ZIP
positions.summary: ValarDragon would cap ZCG's holdings at about $25M and return the excess to the NSM; kworks and gordonesTV propose regional reserves funded from the treasury; strahncryptography points to ebfull's Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund ZIP as the best option.

summary.tldr: ZCG proposes tapering its own block-reward share and sending the rest to the NSM. Replies split between support as a compromise, calls to abolish ZCG or restructure it for accountability, and defenders of independent community funding; disputes over the ZSA poll, ZCG's record and employer motives run hot.
